- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after dips.
- Model often overshoots after recent highs; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model underestimates during strong positive sentiment trends; adjust upward by 1–2% for 3–7 day horizon if sentiment >0.5.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after model peak, apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–4 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward if sentiment is neutral or positive.
